# cloudminator_firewall (Resource)

An inbound allow rule on a subnet, applied on top of the platform's baseline isolation. Changing `subnet_id` replaces the rule; everything else changes in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cloudminator_firewall" "https" {
  name      = "https"
  subnet_id = cloudminator_subnet.app.id
  protocol  = "tcp"
  port      = "443"
  source    = "0.0.0.0/0"
  comment   = "public HTTPS"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name.
- `subnet_id` (String) Subnet the rule applies to.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Free-form comment.
- `org` (String) Organization slug. Defaults to the provider's `org`. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `port` (String) Port (`443`) or range (`8000:8100`). Omit for any port.
- `project` (String) Project slug. Defaults to the provider's `project` (or `default`). Changing it forces a new resource.
- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp` or `icmp`. Omit for any protocol.
- `source` (String) Source CIDR. Omit for any source.
- `tags` (Map of String) Key/value tags. Used by attribute-based access control, so a change can be denied if the new tags fall outside the caller's scope.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned rule id (`fwrule-…`).
- `phase` (String) Lifecycle phase reported by the platform (`Running`, `Stopped`, …).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a firewall rule by organization, project and rule id.
terraform import cloudminator_firewall.https acme/default/fwrule-0123456789abcdef01234567
```
